title: Risk-Based Inspection in India: OISD, PESO and API 580
description: How RBI works within OISD standards, PESO's rules and the 2025 Boilers Act, where India refines, and how Atlantis runs remote RBI studies for Indian sites.
h1: Risk-based inspection for Indian refineries, petrochemical plants and depots
intro: Indian oil and gas facilities work under a dense set of national rulebooks: OISD standards written for the oil industry, PESO's rules for petroleum storage and compressed gas vessels, and a boiler law that was rewritten in 2025. This page is for inspection heads and reliability engineers at Indian refineries, petrochemical plants and depots who want to know how an RBI programme sits within those rules, where the country's refining capacity is concentrated, what the monsoon and the crude slate do to equipment, and how Atlantis delivers an RBI study remotely, including for sites a short distance from its Hyderabad team.

highlights.p: OISD standards, PESO's rules and the boiler regulations set minimum inspection and testing requirements. The study treats those as limits it works inside: a risk ranking can concentrate effort and choose better techniques, but it does not stretch a statutory or OISD date.

Indian refineries plan inspection around major shutdowns that come years apart. The plan says which items must be opened at the next one, which can be monitored on stream until the one after, and what each inspection has to achieve to earn credit in the risk model.

Atlantis works from Hyderabad as well as Houston, so Indian sites share the study team's day in IST. Workshops fit around shift handovers and unit meetings, and the study needs no travel: field checks go to your inspectors or your inspection contractor.

sections.h: The rulebooks an Indian RBI study works within
p: Indian oil and gas facilities answer to more national documents than most. None of them, as far as we have found, makes risk-based inspection compulsory; together they decide how much room an RBI programme has. The industry's own technical directorate writes inspection standards, the petroleum and explosives regulator licenses storage and governs compressed gas vessels, and boilers have a separate statute and inspectorate. On top of that, public sector refiners and private groups keep corporate inspection manuals, and many adopt API and ASME codes alongside the national documents.

Before the data request goes out, the study fixes which of these documents governs each equipment class at the site, and who in the owner's organisation can approve an interval that differs from the default. The table summarises the layers.

sections.h: OISD standards and what they leave to risk
p: OISD publishes standards for the inspection of static equipment, among them OISD-STD-128 for unfired pressure vessels and OISD-STD-129 for storage tanks. In the revision of OISD-STD-128 we reviewed, which dates from 1999, future inspection dates are scheduled from established corrosion rates, the type of service and the remaining corrosion allowance, with fixed requirements on top: every new vessel inspected within its first two years of operation, reactors internally within ten years, skirts inspected after removal of fireproofing at intervals of no more than five years, and the welds of ammonia and LPG storage vessels examined internally by wet fluorescent magnetic particle testing once in ten years besides normal inspection. The standard also states plainly that statutory inspection frequencies must be adhered to.

That structure suits a risk-based approach better than it first appears. A standard that already ties intervals to corrosion rate and remaining allowance is asking for the same inputs an RBI study uses, and the study adds what a corrosion-rate method lacks: damage mechanisms that do not show up as general thinning, such as cracking, high-temperature hydrogen attack or localised attack at injection points, and a measure of how effective past inspections really were. The fixed OISD requirements stay in the plan as hard limits. OISD revises its standards from time to time, so the first step is to confirm the current edition of each one the site applies.

sections.h: PESO licences and compressed gas vessels
p: PESO administers the Petroleum Rules 2002, under which petroleum storage and handling installations are licensed, and the Static and Mobile Pressure Vessels (Unfired) Rules, which govern vessels storing compressed and liquefied gases. For an RBI study the distinction matters. A tank farm's petroleum licence sits beside its tank inspection programme, and where neither the licence nor the rules fix the internal inspection interval, the owner's programme sets it; that is where an API 653 risk basis can be written in. A compressed gas vessel under the pressure vessel rules carries statutory examination and testing that the study records as fixed.

LPG and ammonia storage is where the two approaches meet most often. The statutory test date does not move, but a damage mechanism review can still decide what the examination should concentrate on: wet hydrogen sulfide cracking or ammonia stress corrosion cracking at welds, the condition of supports and legs, external corrosion at the soil interface, and whether the technique used last time could have found any of these. Writing that into the plan ahead of the statutory examination means the outage is used to look for the damage the vessel can actually suffer.

The Boilers Act 2025 came into force on 1 May 2025 and repealed the Boilers Act of 1923. It gives a Central Boilers Board the job of regulating the design, manufacture, erection and use of boilers, with chief inspectors and inspectors exercising the powers each state prescribes. The Indian Boiler Regulations 2026, framed by the Board under the new Act, replace the regulations of 1950. Among other changes they set out how competent persons are authorised and call for a remaining life assessment of boilers after 100,000 operating hours at 400 °C and above, and after 25 years for other boilers.

A refinery's boilers, waste heat boilers and steam-side components therefore sit in a statutory regime of their own. The RBI register lists them with their certificate dates and keeps them out of the risk targets, so they neither inflate nor flatter the ranking of other equipment. Their remaining life assessment reports are still worth reading, because they show how the site has managed creep and high-temperature damage in steam service, which informs the treatment of fired heater tubes and hot process lines elsewhere in the register.

The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas lists twenty-three refineries, owned by public sector companies, joint ventures and private groups. They are spread unevenly. The largest single concentration is Reliance Industries' pair of refineries at Jamnagar; much of the rest sits on the coast where crude arrives, with a group of inland refineries fed by pipeline and a cluster of smaller, older plants in the Northeast. The table groups them by what tends to shape an RBI study rather than by size.

Petrochemical complexes, gas processing plants, LNG import terminals, marketing depots and pipeline terminals sit alongside the refineries and bring their own equipment classes, from crackers and polymer reactors to large crude and product tank farms at the ports.

sections.h: Monsoon, coastline and the crude slate
p: Most of India's refining capacity is coastal, and the south-west monsoon wets insulation, cladding and structures for months at a time before the dry season bakes them. That wet and dry cycling is close to ideal for corrosion under insulation on carbon steel, and coastal sites add chloride deposition that drives external pitting and, on insulated austenitic stainless steel, chloride stress corrosion cracking. Inland refineries see less marine exposure but wide swings between summer and winter temperatures, and dust that holds moisture against steel.

Process damage follows the crude slate and the configuration. Imported crude grades with significant sulfur put high-temperature sulfidation high on the list for crude, vacuum and coker circuits, and some crudes bring naphthenic acid. Hydrotreaters and hydrocrackers carry wet hydrogen sulfide cracking, ammonium bisulfide and ammonium chloride corrosion in the reactor effluent train, and high-temperature hydrogen attack where the steels and operating conditions make it credible. Amine and sour water systems, caustic service and the cooling water network complete a register that, for a large site, runs to a very large number of items and needs a structured damage mechanism review before any risk number means much.

sections.h: Turning paper history into usable inspection data
p: Many Indian refineries have decades of inspection history, much of it in paper reports, scanned files and spreadsheets kept by different groups across different eras. Thickness readings may sit against point numbers that no longer match the isometrics, and older reports record what was done without saying how much of the surface was covered. An RBI model cannot credit an inspection it cannot interpret.

The study therefore starts with data rationalisation. Thickness histories are tied to current CMLs, corrosion rates are calculated with outliers examined rather than averaged away, each historical inspection is graded for the effectiveness its technique and coverage could achieve against the item's damage mechanisms, and anything that cannot be reconciled goes on the data-gap log with a proposed field check. That work often changes the conclusions more than the risk calculation does, because it shows which items have been inspected well and which only appear to have been.
Requests from Indian sites cover the whole life of a programme, from a first assessment to a revalidation.

sections.h: A remote study, even close to home
p: Atlantis works from Houston and Hyderabad, and Hyderabad shares India Standard Time with every Indian site. That makes scheduling simple: workshops can run across the Indian working day, fitted around shift handovers and unit meetings, and follow-up does not wait on another country's office hours. Houston, ten and a half or eleven and a half hours behind depending on the US season, carries review and drafting forward through the Indian night.

Being in the same country does not change how the study is delivered. It runs remotely, from a data room and video workshops, exactly as it would for a site abroad, and it is built to need no travel. Field checks such as insulation condition, injection point locations, dead legs or the state of tank annular plates go on a verification list for your inspectors or your inspection contractor, whose findings return to the model. Keeping the study remote also means a refinery in Assam or Punjab is served in the same way as one in Andhra Pradesh.

Owners who keep design data on internal systems can grant controlled access or run document reviews by screen share. The study logs which documents it has seen, so the basis of every result stays traceable when the register is audited or revalidated.

sections.h: Who approves, and the limits of the study
p: The inspection intervals and tasks the study proposes are approved by the owner's inspection authority, usually the head of the site's inspection department under its inspection manual, or by an API inspector where the owner's procedures call for one. Statutory examinations under PESO's rules and the boiler regulations stay with the authorities and competent persons those rules name. Atlantis prepares the assessment and recommends; it does not act as inspector of record.

Damage found during inspection that falls outside the construction code goes to the owner's engineer for assessment, and the register is updated with the result. Atlantis does not perform fitness-for-service assessments.

faqs.q: Do OISD standards allow risk-based inspection intervals?
faqs.a: The OISD standards we have reviewed schedule inspection from corrosion rates, service and remaining allowance, add fixed requirements for particular equipment and require statutory frequencies to be met. A risk-based plan can work within that framework, refining technique and coverage and setting intervals inside the limits, while the fixed requirements stay as hard dates. Confirm the current edition of each standard and record any departure in the owner's procedure.

faqs.q: Can RBI extend the statutory test of an LPG sphere or bullet?
faqs.a: No. Vessels under PESO's Static and Mobile Pressure Vessels (Unfired) Rules keep their statutory examination and testing dates. What the study adds is a damage mechanism basis and an inspection specification for that examination, so the outage looks for the cracking and corrosion the vessel is actually exposed to, and the technique chosen earns credit in the risk model afterwards.

faqs.q: Are boilers included in the RBI study?
faqs.a: They are listed in the register as statutory items under the Boilers Act 2025 and the Indian Boiler Regulations, with their certificate and inspection dates, but they are kept out of the risk targets. Their remaining life assessment records are still reviewed, because they show how creep and high-temperature damage have been managed on the site, which is useful context for fired heaters and hot process lines.

faqs.q: Will the Hyderabad team come to our refinery?
faqs.a: The study is designed so that it does not need to. The engineering runs from your documents and from video workshops on IST, and anything that has to be seen on the equipment goes on a verification list for your inspectors or your inspection contractor. Their findings are fed back into the model, and the study records who verified each item and when.

faqs.q: Our history is mostly on paper. Is RBI still possible?
faqs.a: Yes, but the first phase is data work rather than risk calculation. Readings are tied to current CMLs, corrosion rates recalculated, each past inspection graded for effectiveness, and gaps logged with proposed field checks. The early register is conservative where data are missing, and it becomes sharper as each shutdown adds inspection results of known quality.

faqs.q: Which RBI method will the study use?
faqs.a: The one your inspection manual names. Where the owner follows API RP 580 and API RP 581, or a corporate RBI standard built on them, the study follows it. Where no standard exists yet, a semi-quantitative approach is usually the practical starting point, with quantitative assessment reserved for the equipment where consequence is highest and the data support it.

faqs.q: How does the study handle monsoon-driven CUI?
faqs.a: By ranking the insulated population before the inspection plan is written. Operating temperature, insulation and cladding type and condition, coating history, age and exposure to rain and sea air decide the risk band, and each band gets an approach, from targeted insulation removal to screening and corrosion mapping, timed where possible for the dry season or the next outage.

The head of your inspection department, or whoever your inspection manual names as the authority for intervals. The study supplies the basis for each interval and its reassessment triggers, so approval can be given item by item with the evidence in front of the approver. Statutory dates under PESO's rules and the boiler regulations are not affected by the study.
